title: Shop Smart
subtitle: Shopping, prices and choices in Calder Vale

parts.title: Sale, returns and delivery notices
parts.instructions: For each notice, choose what it means.
notices: CALDER VALE HOME STORE: Our winter sale ends this Sunday at 5 p.m. Everything in the lamp and rug department is half price while stocks last.
RETURNS: Goods can be brought back within 28 days with a receipt. Without a receipt we can only offer a gift card. Items must be unworn, with labels still attached.
CAI: Flatmate, tracking says my parcel was delivered at 11, but I can’t find it anywhere. I’m in meetings until six. Could you look behind the bins and in the porch when you get in?
NEW AT MARKET FOODS: Scan your shopping with our app as you walk round, then pay at the self-service desk by the exit. No more queues! Ask a member of staff if you need help setting up.
THANK YOU FOR YOUR ORDER! Use code SAVE10 on your next purchase to get ten per cent off. The code works online only and ends on 30 June. It cannot be used with other offers.

questions.prompt: What does the notice say about the sale?
options: Only the rugs are cheaper now.
questions.explanation: The winter sale ends on Sunday at 5 p.m., so it finishes at the weekend. Lamps as well as rugs are half price, and the sale is already running.

questions.prompt: What can a customer do without a receipt?
options: Get the money back in cash.
Swap the item for another size.
questions.explanation: Without a receipt the shop can only offer a gift card, so the customer cannot have cash or an exchange.

questions.prompt: What does Cai want his flatmate to do?
options: Search around the house for the parcel.
Call the delivery company at lunchtime.
Collect the parcel from a nearby shop.
questions.explanation: Cai cannot find the parcel and asks his flatmate to look behind the bins and in the porch when they get home.

questions.prompt: What are shoppers told they can do?
options: Pay without waiting in a long line.
Order their food before they arrive.
questions.explanation: Customers scan items with the app and pay at a self-service desk by the exit, so they avoid a long wait at the till.

questions.prompt: What must customers do to get the discount?
options: Spend at least ten pounds in a shop.
Enter a code when they buy online.
Show this message at the shop till.
questions.explanation: The code SAVE10 works online only, so customers have to type it in when they buy on the website.

parts.title: Saving up for a new bike
parts.instructions: Read the text and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last spring my old bike finally fell apart, and I decided to buy a better one. The one I wanted cost almost three hundred pounds, which is a lot when you only have pocket money and a little from a weekend job. My dad said he would pay half for my birthday, but I felt I should try to save the money on my own.

I started by writing down everything I spent for a month. I was shocked. Nearly a quarter of my money went on snacks, drinks and small things I did not really need. I also sold some old games, a pair of trainers and my guitar, which I had hardly touched since I was twelve. That brought in almost eighty pounds.

After four months, I had enough, and I went to the shop on a Saturday, feeling very pleased with myself. The assistant told me that the model I wanted was last year’s, and that the new colours would arrive in a few weeks, so the price would drop. She suggested I wait. It was hard to be patient, but I did, and in the end I paid forty pounds less.

I ride the bike to school every day now. I am proud of it, and I am much more careful about where my money goes.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer decide to save the money herself?
options: Her father refused to give her anything.
She wanted to manage without help.
The shop gave discounts for savers.
questions.explanation: Her dad offered to pay half, but she felt she should save the money on her own.

questions.prompt: What did she find when she wrote down her spending?
options: Most of her money went on clothes.
She spent more on clothes than anything else.
She was already saving a lot each month.
A lot of money went on small things.
questions.explanation: She was shocked that nearly a quarter of her money went on snacks, drinks and small things she did not need.

questions.prompt: How did she get extra money?
options: By selling things she no longer used.
By walking dogs for her neighbours.
By working in a shop at the weekend.
By getting a loan from her dad.
questions.explanation: She sold old games, trainers and her guitar, which she had hardly used.

questions.prompt: Why did she wait before buying the bike?
options: She still did not have enough money yet.
The shop was about to close down.
She learned that it would soon be cheaper.
The bike she wanted was not in the shop.
questions.explanation: The assistant said the new colours would arrive in a few weeks and the price of last year’s model would drop.

questions.prompt: How does the writer feel now?
options: Sorry that she did not buy it sooner.
Proud, and more careful with money.
Worried about the cost of the repairs.
Happy that her father paid half.
questions.explanation: She says she is proud of the bike and much more careful about where her money goes.

parts.title: A week of online shopping
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Last month, our consumer studies teacher set us an unusual project: to spend a week shopping online for a present that cost less than twenty pounds, and then report back to the class. I thought it would be simple because I order things on the internet all the time. [1] I had already looked at six different websites by Monday evening.

My first problem was choosing. I wanted a present for my grandmother, who loves puzzles. [2] Some had four stars, others had four and a half, and the information all seemed to say the same thing. In the end, I decided to read the customers’ comments properly.

That helped a lot. [3] One reviewer said the pieces were so small that her father needed a magnifying glass. I chose a puzzle with larger pieces.

When I compared prices, I noticed that delivery was sometimes very expensive. [4] That would have taken me over my budget, so I picked a site with free delivery on orders over fifteen pounds.

The parcel arrived on Friday, a day before the deadline. [5] The lesson I took from the week was simple: slow down before you click “buy”.
sentences: Some of my classmates chose to buy books or sweets instead.
My grandmother loved it and finished it in two evenings.
Several people had written about details that the product pages left out.
One website wanted ten pounds to send a puzzle that cost twelve.
There were dozens of puzzles, and they all looked almost the same.
One of my friends bought a pair of trainers that were too big.
It turned out to be much harder than I expected.
Some websites send emails every day with special offers.

gaps.explanation: “It turned out to be much harder than I expected” contrasts with “I thought it would be simple” and explains why she had already visited six websites.
“There were dozens of puzzles” explains “Some had four stars, others had four and a half”: “Some” and “others” refer to the puzzles.
The comments “helped a lot” because people wrote about details missing from the product pages; the next sentence gives one example.
Ten pounds delivery for a twelve-pound puzzle is the example, and “That would have taken me over my budget” refers to it.
After the parcel arrives, the grandmother’s reaction to the present comes naturally before the final lesson. Sentence F is about classmates and fits no gap.

parts.title: Buying new trainers
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: My old trainers had a hole in one side, so they were no longer [1] for running, and I decided to buy a new pair. At the first shop, the assistant [2] my feet and told me I needed a bigger size than I thought. I tried on six pairs, but they were all too [3] for me. In the second shop, I found some in the sale that were half [4]. They felt very comfortable, so I took them to the [5] and paid by card. When I got home, I saw that they were a different colour from the photo on the website, but I decided to [6] them anyway.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: “Suitable for running” is the correct collocation; the shoes had a hole, so they were no longer right for the job.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: A shoe-shop assistant measures your feet to find your size; you do not weigh, count or press them.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: “Too expensive for me” fits the shopper’s budget; “too careful”, “too healthy” and “too useful” make no sense for shoes that she rejects.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: “Half price” is the fixed expression for a sale reduction of fifty per cent.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: You take what you want to buy to the till and pay there.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: “Keep them anyway” means she decided not to take them back even though the colour was different.

parts.title: A message about a jacket to return
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Hi Andres,
I bought this jacket [1] Saturday, but it is [2] big that the sleeves cover my hands. Could you come with [3] to the shop tomorrow after lunch? I [4] the receipt in my bag, so they should give me my money back. If they do [5] have a smaller size, I will choose something [6] instead. I really like the colour, but I do not want to spend money on a jacket I cannot wear.
Thanks!
Vera

gaps.explanation: We use “on” with a day of the week: “on Saturday”.
“So big that” introduces the result: the sleeves cover her hands.
“Come with me” needs an object pronoun after the preposition.
She still has the receipt, so “I have the receipt”.
“If they do not have” is the negative form after “do”.
“Something else instead” means a different jacket if there is no smaller size.

parts.title: Short conversations in shops
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: jakub
turns.text: Hi, can I help you?

turns.speaker: livia
turns.text: I bought this jacket yesterday, but it’s a bit tight across the shoulders.

turns.speaker: jakub

turns.speaker: livia
turns.text: Not really, I love the red. I just need more room. To be honest, I was thinking of going to the shop across the road, because they sell something similar. But I like this one better.

turns.speaker: jakub
turns.text: Then I’ll check the stock room for you.

turns.speaker: livia
turns.text: Do you have this one in a size up? I think a large would be perfect.

turns.speaker: jakub
turns.text: One moment, I’ll have a look.

question.explanation: She likes the red colour and prefers this jacket to the one in the other shop, but it is tight, so she asks if there is a larger size.

turns.speaker: norman
turns.text: Hello, this is Norman from Dalton Electronics, calling Efua about the speaker. You saw it online for sixty pounds last week, and today the shop price is seventy-five. I know it looks strange, so I checked the till, and it’s correct, there’s no mistake. The sale ended on Sunday, and now it’s the normal price again. The new model arrives next month and will cost ninety, but it’s not in the shop yet. If you can come before the weekend, I might ask my manager for a small discount. Thank you, and have a nice day.

turns.speaker: konrad
turns.text: I’m sorry, but I need proof that you bought this printer in the last year.

turns.speaker: sade

turns.speaker: sade
turns.text: They closed last month, I’m afraid. But I paid by card. I can show you my bank statement on my phone.

turns.speaker: konrad

options: By showing the box it came in
By phoning the shop to ask

turns.speaker: marley
turns.text: Hi Tunde, it’s Marley. I’m in town with the voucher you gave me for my birthday, thank you again! I asked at the till if they could give me the cash instead, but they said vouchers can’t be changed for money. I thought about keeping it until next month, when the new collection arrives, but it ends in three weeks and I’d probably forget. Anyway, there’s a lovely pair of brown boots in the window, the ones with the thick soles. They cost a bit more than the voucher, but I can pay the difference. I’m going in to try them now. Talk later!

Keep it until next month or later

turns.speaker: oisin
turns.text: Hello, Pine Furniture. Can I help you?

turns.speaker: sinead
turns.text: I’m calling about the grey sofa I ordered. The website said it would arrive on Thursday morning.

turns.speaker: oisin
turns.text: Let me see. Yes, that was the first date, but our lorry is full on Thursday, and the afternoon is also taken. I can offer you Friday afternoon, between one and four.

turns.speaker: sinead
turns.text: Friday morning would be better for me, I’m at work in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: oisin
turns.text: I’m afraid that’s not possible. Is somebody at home?

turns.speaker: sinead

turns.speaker: oisin

question.prompt: When will the sofa be delivered?
question.explanation: Thursday is full both in the morning and in the afternoon, and the morning of Friday is not possible, so the sofa will come on Friday afternoon.

turns.speaker: soraya
turns.text: Look at this queue. There are only two people working at the cashier desk.

turns.speaker: zubair
turns.text: We could use the machines on the left. They’re free.

turns.text: I tried them last time and the screen froze. It took ten minutes.

turns.speaker: zubair
turns.text: Then let’s go to the supermarket near the station.

turns.speaker: soraya
turns.text: That’s a long walk, and we’re only buying five things. The queue is moving quickly.

turns.speaker: zubair
turns.text: True. And look, another cashier has just arrived.

turns.speaker: soraya
turns.text: Good. Let’s stay here and join the line. I only need to pay and go home, I’m so tired today.

turns.speaker: zubair

turns.speaker: soraya
turns.text: Yes, please!

options: Use the machines on the left

turns.speaker: ruairi
turns.text: Hi Holly, it’s Ruairi. I’m in the shoe shop and I’m in trouble. I came to buy brown shoes, because you said they go with everything. But the brown ones look old-fashioned on me. I nearly left without buying anything, because they’re all so expensive. Then the assistant showed me a pair of black ones that are half price, and they look smart for the wedding. So I’m taking those. They’re a bit shiny, but I think you will like them. I’ll show you tonight when I get home, and then you can tell me the truth. Bye!

question.explanation: He planned brown shoes and nearly bought nothing, but the black pair is half price and looks smart, so he buys them.

parts.title: What is the main point?

turns.speaker: dagmar

turns.speaker: cristian

turns.text: Don’t spend money yet. Take them back to the shop and ask for a free replacement. They have to do that when something breaks so soon.

parts.title: A talk about a shop’s loyalty scheme
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good morning, everyone. I’m Gopal, the manager of Brook Street Stores here in Calder Vale, and I’d like to tell you about our new loyalty scheme. It’s free to join. You can fill in a form online, but most people prefer to come into the shop and sign up at the customer service desk, which is next to the main door. Not at the tills, because the cashiers are too busy. Once you’re a member, you get a card, and you show it every time you shop. You earn one point for each pound that you spend. We thought about one point for every two pounds, but that seemed too mean. Every month we count your points and send you vouchers. Some shops send them by post, but we use email, so please give us your address, and check your spam folder. The vouchers come in the first week of the month. Now for the nice things. On your birthday, you receive a present: a free coffee in our cafe. Last year it was a cake, but many members told us they would prefer a coffee, so we changed it. Another bonus is that you get double points every Wednesday. It used to be on Fridays, but those are our busiest days. You can use the card in our two other shops in the valley as well, so your points grow quicker. Finally, a warning. Your points don’t last forever. They don’t disappear in the middle of the year, but they do run out at the end of the year, so use your vouchers before then. A friend of mine lost ninety points last December, and she was not happy! So, I hope you will join us. Thank you for listening, and are there any questions?

gaps.prompt: To join the scheme, go to the customer service ___
gaps.explanation: You sign up at the customer service desk next to the main door, not at the tills.

gaps.prompt: Members earn one ___ for each pound they spend
gaps.explanation: One point for each pound; one point for every two pounds was the first idea but it seemed mean.
They use email, not post, and the vouchers come in the first week of the month.

gaps.prompt: The birthday present for members is a free ___
gaps.explanation: The present is a free coffee; last year it was a cake.
Double points are on Wednesday; it used to be Friday.

gaps.prompt: Points run out at the ___ of the year

parts.title: An interview with a young shop owner
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Divya, what gave you the idea for your shop?

turns.speaker: divya
turns.text: Honestly, it wasn’t a teacher, though my art teacher always said I should start a business. And I didn’t copy anyone. I’ve never seen a shop like this abroad. It started in my kitchen. One day I noticed how much plastic my family threw away in a week: bottles, bags, boxes. I was shocked. A full bin every two days! I thought, there must be a better way to buy soap and rice.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you pay for the business?

turns.speaker: divya
turns.text: The bank said no, because I was only nineteen, and nobody wanted to lend me money. My parents offered a bit, but I said thanks, I want to do this on my own. So I used what I had earned from two years of Saturday jobs in a bakery. It wasn’t a fortune, but it was enough for the shelves and the first products.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Why were the first months so hard?

turns.speaker: divya
turns.text: People did come in, which surprised me. Customers were curious from day one. And I knew exactly what to sell, I had a long list. The problem was that I did everything myself. I opened at eight, cleaned, ordered, did the accounts, closed at seven, and then more paperwork at home. I was exhausted. I cried a few times, I have to say.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you keep customers coming back?

turns.speaker: divya
turns.text: Not with low prices, I can’t compete there. And I do post photos online, but only twice a week, it takes too much time. What works is that I know my customers. I remember that Mr Evans likes his tea very strong, and that one lady needs gluten-free flour. They feel special, and they come back.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What do you do about big supermarkets with lower prices?

turns.speaker: divya
turns.text: I tried to match their prices at the beginning, and I lost money. I would love a second shop, but not yet. Now I do something different: I give advice. People ask me how to cook with lentils or how to store spices, and I explain. A supermarket cashier can’t do that.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What do you want to do next year?

turns.speaker: divya
turns.text: Many people say I should open another shop in the next town, and perhaps one day, but I’m not ready. And I don’t want a manager, I like being in the shop. What I want is a delivery service. Lots of my customers are older or very busy, and they’d love to get their shopping at the door. I’m already looking for a small electric van.
